title: Options Market-Making Lab
summary: An educational Python simulator for exploring options pricing, discrete hedging, and inventory risk.
question: What changes when an options hedge can only be adjusted at discrete times and every adjustment has a cost?

figure.alt: Simulated transaction fees of $0.016 for 12 hedge trades, $0.034 for 52, and $0.065 for 252.
figure.caption: In the six-month call example, fees range from 1.6¢ to 6.5¢ across three schedules. Trade counts include opening the hedge.

symbol.name: delta
symbol.meaning: how much an option’s price moves with the stock, and the quantity the hedge tracks.

sections.title: What’s in the simulator
sections.text: I priced European options three ways: Black–Scholes, a binomial tree, and Monte Carlo. Then I simulated adjusting the stock hedge as the option’s sensitivity changed. In a separate market-making simulation, the dealer lowers its quotes when it has too many options, encouraging buyers to take some of that inventory.

sections.title: What the example measures
sections.text: Each schedule runs on its own seeded price path. The bars show the commissions paid on stock trades in those runs. To isolate the effect of trading more often, I’d compare the schedules on the same underlying price paths across many runs.
